slots.hypothesis: Deep-dig the comovement core that GP independently evolved into the library's current best head (+1.18, cross_max(cross_mean(day_corr(Ret,Volume),3),60) after stripping a redundant monotonic add-wrapper that the dissection ablation showed contributes 0). 13 seeds across 6 mechanism groups: frequency-vs-magnitude of positive/negative comovement days (is_gt0/is_lt0 60d share), surprise/extremes relative to the stock's own history (cross_max/cross_min minus cross_mean), regime migration and stability (5d-60d diff, cross_stddev), minute-sign asymmetry (whole-day corr minus up-minute-only / down-minute-only corr, each still containing the core verbatim via sub()), volatility-weighted informativeness (mul with day_std(Ret)), and two necessity/robustness baselines (bare cross_mean(.,3), and a cleaner cross_max window-30 variant). Goal: resolve whether the alpha is in the level/magnitude of comovement or its frequency/extremity, and clarify the sign (round-1 predicted negative/chasing-reversal, but the discovered head's sign is +1, unresolved).

Fresh idea inspired by this round's price-volume findings but using order-imbalance rather than correlation: Partura's own day_signed_ratio(Ret, Amt) (never evaluated anywhere in this seed's library) measures net directional turnover share in [-1,1], grounded in Chordia-Subrahmanyam order-imbalance literature and Easley-O'Hara trade-size-informativeness literature. 13 seeds: level/smoothing (raw, 20d/60d mean), money- vs share-weighted imbalance and their difference, stability (cross_stddev), migration (5d-60d diff), board/listing-age neutralization, and a morning-vs-afternoon session split (via in_half) echoing round 1's retail-open/institutional-close structural hypothesis but measured through buying pressure instead of volume timing.

result.summary:
Acted as PI for seed 805, round 2 of the Partura/AlphaCube C08 cold-start coldstart experiment (arm P). Read rules.md §1-5, r2/loc.md + r2/loc.json (3 heads, 311 archived candidates, enrichment table, mechanical core cards, dissection ablation with 21 paid evaluations, no R candidates flagged by the tool itself), r2/R_prev.json (empty), notebook.md (round 1 beliefs/predictions), and round 1's missions_final.yaml + audit_record.json + analysis.md + lit.md + shadow.yaml for context (both round-1 slots passed audit on the first attempt; the N requirement across 3 rounds is already satisfied by round 1).

Key structural reading: round 2's snapshot has 3 heads. The strongest (+1.18) was produced by GP's own evolution from the round-1 N idea (day_corr(Ret,Volume) family); its dissection ablation shows an outer add(5,X)+X wrapper contributes nothing (pure rank-preserving redundancy) and the real skeleton is cross_max(cross_mean(day_corr(Ret,Volume),3),60). The other two heads (+0.93, +0.83) extend round 1's day_centroid(Volume) E slot. Critically, the dissection already paid to knock out the "auction-tilt" sub-term inside the +0.83 head and found the clean cross_mean(day_centroid(Volume),30) alone scores +1.73 (necessity -0.91, i.e. that sub-component is actively harmful) — a textbook R candidate. A separate enrichment-only family (day_pos_ratio(High)/day_first(High)/LogFloatShares, via cs_last_low20) was deliberately NOT used as an E core: day_pos_ratio(High) is almost certainly a near-constant panel (share of minutes with High>0, and price is essentially always positive), making it a likely disguised LogFloatShares proxy and a math-problem/degeneracy risk under the audit's §4 criteria.

Wrote /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/research/coldstart_C08/partura/s805/r2/missions.yaml with:
- Slot a (E, core 'day_corr(Ret, Volume)', first E-use of this core — round 1 used N not E for it): 13 seeds in 6 mechanism groups (frequency vs magnitude, surprise/extremes vs own history, migration/stability, minute-sign asymmetry, volatility-weighted informativeness, necessity baselines), each verified to literally contain the core subtree. 4 literature citations (Kyle 1985; Chen-Hong-Stein 2001; Avramov-Chordia-Goyal 2006; Gervais-Kaniel-Mingelgrin 2001).
- Slot b (N, new idea, no fixed core): Partura's own day_signed_ratio(Ret,Amt) order-imbalance operator (never used anywhere in this seed's history), 13 seeds, grounded in Chordia-Subrahmanyam 2004, Easley-O'Hara 1987, Admati-Pfleiderer 1988, Chordia-Roll-Subrahmanyam 2002.
- R: 1 group targeting head 'cross_mean(sub(day_centroid(Volume), day_centroid(delete_open_close(Volume))), 30)' with 3 variants (windows 15/30/60 of the clean cross_mean(day_centroid(Volume), d)), justified directly from the already-computed dissection ablation evidence.

Every expression was pre-validated against the project's own parser/canonicalizer (partura.steer / alphacube.parser, matching c06_check.py's own logic) before being written, including an explicit core-containment check (tree-node key equality) for every E seed — this caught and fixed an initial design mistake (three up/down-minute-asymmetry seeds that applied day_corr to a transformed Ret and so did NOT contain the literal core; rewritten as sub(day_corr(Ret,Volume), day_corr(mul(Ret,is_gt0/is_lt0(Ret)),Volume)) to fix it).

Appended a "第 2 轮" section to /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/research/coldstart_C08/partura/s805/notebook.md: updated beliefs (day_centroid axis confirmed but driven by "timing mismatch"/"auction tilt" periphery rather than the "habit vs event" framing I'd guessed in round 1; day_corr(Ret,Volume) looks like a possibly stronger independent axis, with the discovered head's sign being positive — contradicting my round-1 reversal hypothesis, flagged as this round's open question; High-price family flagged as a likely proxy, deliberately not pursued), ex-ante predictions for both new slots and the R group, and an honest scoring of round 1's 4 predictions (bare-core score ≈0.44 confirmed exactly; "all controls <0.5" confirmed but "max is LogFloatCap" was wrong — it's actually the known-family control at 0.20 vs LogFloatCap's 0.07; which E periphery group would win was wrong — timing-mismatch/auction-tilt beat the habit/level group I favored; the auction-tilt sub-term's own weakness was correctly anticipated in direction but its standalone score (-0.30) and its role as an active drag on the head (not just low contribution) were stronger than expected; N slot's magnitude prediction (≥0.5) was right but its direction (negative/reversal) was wrong since the realized head has sign +1).
